newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast light crudes end higher with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast light crudes end higher with NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes ended higher Monday, tracking a NYMEX market lifted by Artic cold in Europe, traders said.
NYMEX crude for February delivery settled 15 cents higher at $25.37 a barrel on the back of a gas oil rally in London's futures market.
But the spot market for West Coast light crudes remained quiet, with most traders out for the Christmas and New Year's holidays.
Traders said a 600,000 barrel shipment of Koch Alberta crude would load January 15 - 17 in Canada, and arrive at a Chevron refinery several days later.
The grade is a typical substitute for Alaskan North Slope (ANS) crude, which has a API gravity of 27 degrees.
Players who supposedly closed the deal declined comment or were not immediately available.
After an early rise, ANS crude held its 15-cent gain over Friday's market. It followed the increase in West Texas Intermediate, the benchmark grade.
The ANS discount stayed $1.70 below WTI, unchanged from a December 13 sale. The combination of higher WTI and flat discounts left ANS prices between $23.55/23.75 a barrel.
Kern River prices stayed at $18.65/18.75 a barrel after companies lifted postings late last week.
Discounts remained 10 cents below to even with postings, traders said.
Line 63 crude remained untraded off WTI, while the posting plus market was notionally $0.95 to $1.05.
